title: Bridge Engineering Course at Kunming University of Science and Technology: Detailed Explanation of Bridge Deck Construction
description: The course introduces the layout and construction of bridge decks, focusing on bridge deck pavement, waterproofing and drainage systems, expansion joints, sidewalks, railings, guardrails, lighting poles, and other safety facilities. Bridge deck pavement serves as a protective layer for the main bridge structure and must provide rutting resistance, driving comfort, skid resistance, wear resistance, low-temperature crack resistance, impermeability, and adequate rigidity. Common materials include cement concrete and asphalt concrete with waterproof layers. The course also explains waterproofing-layer construction methods and how suitable structural design can extend bridge deck service life and improve driving safety.

title: Functions and Design of Bridge Deck Waterproofing and Drainage Systems
description: Bridge deck waterproofing and drainage systems protect the bridge structure from moisture damage and help ensure traffic safety. The waterproofing layer intercepts and redirects rainwater away from the bridge deck, reducing deterioration and extending the bridge's service life. Effective drainage design considers the longitudinal and transverse slopes of the deck, the placement of drainage pipes and outlets, and coordination with the bridge structure and surrounding drainage conditions. Expansion joints must also allow the bridge to expand and contract freely while maintaining structural integrity and safety, with attention to waterproofing, drainage, and maintenance requirements.

title: Different Expansion Joints and Pedestrian Walkway Designs for Urban Bridges
description: Bridge expansion joints include butt-joint, shear-joint, and steel-supported types, along with continuous and seamless expansion joints. Continuous bridge deck construction reduces the number of expansion joints and can improve driving comfort. Seamless bridge designs eliminate joints at piers through methods such as integral pier caps, thereby improving structural continuity. Urban bridges must also provide pedestrian walkways whose width is determined by pedestrian traffic volume. Safety belts serve a similar function to pedestrian walkways but are narrower.

title: Bridge Design and Safety Protection
description: As public safety awareness has increased, bridge safety protection facilities have become an essential part of bridge design. Railings should be strong, durable, economical, and visually appropriate, with different height requirements for pedestrian walkways and bicycle lanes. Railings near expansion joints must be able to deform freely while maintaining safety and appearance. Urban and suburban bridges generally require lighting to improve nighttime traffic safety. Highway bridges must include roadside and median barriers to prevent pedestrians, animals, and non-motorized vehicles from entering the highway area while guiding vehicles and protecting drivers. Based on their protective performance, bridge railings are classified as rigid, semi-rigid, or flexible.
